## NAME jev-code - typed routing, decision programs, and validated formal trees driven by Jev, the decision-only model from [typesafe.ai](https://typesafe.ai) ## SDK `jev-code` is first a Jev-only TypeScript library. Applications supply finite alternatives and keep ownership of effects; Jev selects among those alternatives. The public ESM API provides validated decision sessions, typed routers, immutable `DecisionProgram` values, and bounded formal-tree construction. The coding harness and CLI are built on the same contracts. ```typescript import { DecisionSession, defineRouter, route } from 'jev-code'; const router = defineRouter({ inspect: route('Read state without changing it', { effect: 'read' } as const), modify: route('Change application state', { effect: 'write' } as const), }); const selected = await router.select( new DecisionSession(provider), { request: 'Show the current status' }, 'Choose the application route.', ); ``` See [the SDK guide](docs/sdk.md) and the executable [router](examples/router.ts) and [dependency-tree](examples/dependency-tree.ts) examples. Import from the package root; implementation paths are intentionally private. ## CLI SYNOPSIS ``` jev-code [options] ["task"] jev-code --print "task" jev-code decide "question" --choices a,b,c jev-code decide --true "statement" [--threshold p] [--lines] jev-code decide --score "criteria" [--lines] jev-code decide --spec file.json jev-code replay run-id [--speed x] [--plain] jev-code login | logout jev-code ast install module | ast list | ast remove id ``` ## EXAMPLE A live run. Jev builds `stats.py`, reads a numeric data file, computes a summary, runs the program, and reports the observed result.

Play the same recording in your terminal: ```bash asciinema play docs/media/session.cast ``` ## INSTALL ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhighs/jev-code/main/install.sh | bash export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ``` The installer runs on macOS and Linux. It uses Node.js 22 or newer when present. If not, it installs a private Node.js 24 runtime. Run the installer again to update. ## DESCRIPTION Jev does not write text. Jev selects one option from a list, or gives a probability, or gives a score. jev-code turns coding into a sequence of such selections. It builds Python as an abstract syntax tree, one production at a time. It builds Bash commands the same way. It runs the result and shows the outcome. The interactive session is a transcript of cards. Each tool call is one card: a file write, an edit, or a command run. A live pane under the transcript shows the file while Jev builds it. A decision strip shows the current slot, the selected production, and its confidence. A shell command waits for one key: `y` allows it once, `n` denies it, `a` allows the tool for the session. `decide` uses the same model on standard input. A shell script can branch on the exit code without parsing. ## FIRST RUN The first interactive run asks for your typesafe.ai API key. jev-code saves the key in `~/.config/jev-code/config.json` with mode 600. ```bash jev-code ``` `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the environment overrides the saved key. Non-interactive commands do not ask. They stop with a message that names `jev-code login`. ## COMMANDS | Command | Function | | --- | --- | | `jev-code` | Start an interactive session in the current directory. | | `jev-code "task"` | Start a session and submit the task at once. | | `jev-code --print "task"` | Run one task, print the cards to stderr and the summary to stdout, then exit. | | `jev-code --json --print "task"` | Emit one JSON event per line on stdout. | | `jev-code decide ...` | Make one Jev decision over stdin. See DECIDE. | | `jev-code replay ` | Render a saved journal through the same transcript. | | `jev-code login` | Enter the API key and save it. | | `jev-code logout` | Remove the saved API key. | | `jev-code ast install ` | Install an AST adapter module from a local path or an npm package. | | `jev-code ast list` | List the installed AST adapters. | | `jev-code ast remove ` | Remove an installed AST adapter. | | `jev-code --help` | Print all options. | Session commands, typed at the prompt: | Command | Function | | --- | --- | | `/help` | List the session commands. | | `/status` | Show workspace, model, permissions, standing grants, and activity. | | `/files` | List the files written in this session. | | `/show ` | Print a file from the workspace. | | `/trace [n]` | List the last n decisions with their alternatives. Default 10, maximum 20. | | `/plan` | Show the plan Jev recorded. | | `/history` | List the tasks of this session with their outcomes. | | `/permissions ask` | Confirm each shell command. Revokes all `a` grants. | | `/permissions auto` | Run shell commands without confirmation. | | `/paste` | Enter a multi-line task. `/end` submits it. | | `/cancel` | Stop the current run. | | `/clear` | Start a new conversation. Keeps the files. | | `!` | Run a shell command on the host and show it as a card. | | `/exit` | Leave the session. | ## LANGUAGES Every language below is built in. jev-code selects the grammar from the file extension, or from the language named in the task. | Language | Extensions | Grammar | Validator | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Python | `.py` | Full builder: functions, loops, conditions, calls, lists, imports, helper units in parallel, multi-file packages. | `python3` compile | | Bash | commands | Program, arguments, pipes, redirects, `&&`, `\|\|`, `;`. | `bash -n` | | JavaScript | `.js` `.mjs` `.cjs` `.jsx` | Shared imperative core: variables, functions, if/else, while, counted and foreach loops, lists, index, arithmetic, comparison, string join. | TypeScript compiler | | TypeScript | `.ts` `.tsx` `.mts` `.cts` | Same core, typed declarations. | TypeScript compiler | | C | `.c` | Same core, typed. `long`, `const char *`, `bool`; functions before `main`. | `gcc -fsyntax-only` or `clang` | | Rust | `.rs` | Same core, typed. `i64`, `&str`, `bool`; `let mut`. | `rustc --emit=metadata` | | Go | `.go` | Same core, typed. `int`, `string`, `bool`; `_ = x` after each declaration. | `go vet` | | Lua | `.lua` | Same core. 1-based index, `goto continue`. | `luac -p` | | Ruby | `.rb` | Same core. `puts`, `each`, `next`. | `ruby -c` | | Other | any | Install an adapter module. Files without an adapter use bounded text choices. | adapter | A validator must be on `PATH` before Jev writes a file in that language. A missing validator stops the write with a message that names the tool. Each rendered program of the shared core is checked by its real toolchain: a fuzz suite in `test/lang-fuzz.test.ts` drives every dialect with random productions and compiles the result. ## DECIDE `decide` reads all of stdin, asks Jev one question, prints the answer, and exits. It never runs tools. It never writes files. | Form | Output | Exit status | | --- | --- | --- | | `decide "q" --choices a,b,c` | `label confidence` | Index of the selected label. 2 to 100 labels. | | `decide --true "statement" [--threshold 0.5]` | Probability, two decimals. | 0 at or above the threshold. 1 below it. | | `decide --score "criteria"` | Expected level over a four-level rubric, with its label. | 0 | | `... --lines` | One request per stdin line. Lines ranked best first as `valueline`. | 0 | | `decide --spec file.json` | One JSON line per question. | 0 | | `... --json` | Each answer as a `decision` event, the same shape a run emits. | As above. | | `... --truncate` | Decide on the head of an oversized input instead of stopping. | As above. | Failures exit 125: no key, bad arguments, an input that does not fit without `--truncate`, or a provider error. The reason goes to stderr. ## EXAMPLES Basic forms. ```bash # Commit only when Jev agrees. The && chain reads the exit status. git diff | jev-code decide --true "the change is safe to commit" && git commit -am "wip" # One label, one probability, one exit code. echo "Traceback (most recent call last): ValueError" | jev-code decide "Is this an error?" --choices yes,no # yes 1.00 exit 0 # Grade one file. jev-code decide --score "explains why, not only what" < README.md # 1.73 mostly satisfies ``` Route by exit status. The index of the selected label is the exit status. ```bash git log -1 --format=%B | jev-code decide "What kind of change is this?" --choices feature,fix,refactor,docs case $? in 0) label=feature ;; 1) label=fix ;; 2) label=refactor ;; 3) label=docs ;; 125) echo "undecided" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac ``` Move files to the team that owns them. Bash arrays index by exit status. ```bash dirs=(billing support sales) for f in inbox/*.txt; do jev-code decide "Who should handle this message?" --choices billing,support,sales < "$f" code=$? [ "$code" -lt 3 ] && mv "$f" "${dirs[$code]}/" done ``` Filter log lines. `--lines` scores each line once. `--threshold` keeps the lines at or above it. ```bash tail -n 500 app.log | jev-code decide --true "this line reports a failure" --lines --threshold 0.7 # 0.98 ERROR db connection refused ``` Rank technical debt. The highest score comes first. ```bash rg -n "TODO|FIXME" src | jev-code decide --score "urgent: blocks users or risks data" --lines | head -5 # 2.44 src/tools.ts:88: FIXME: crashes when the file is empty # 0.01 src/cli.ts:12: TODO: remove debug print # 0.00 src/diff.ts:5: TODO: rename variable ``` Review a diff with several questions at once. `--spec` runs every question over the same input. ```bash cat > review.json <<'EOF' [ { "question": "Which area does the diff touch most?", "choices": ["api", "ui", "build", "docs"] }, { "true": "the diff adds or updates tests for what it changes", "threshold": 0.6 }, { "score": "the diff is small and focused" } ] EOF git diff main... | jev-code decide --spec review.json | jq -c '{q: .question, a: (.choice // .score), p: .probability}' # {"q":"Which area does the diff touch most?","a":"api","p":null} # {"q":"the diff adds or updates tests for what it changes","a":"true","p":0.98} # {"q":"the diff is small and focused","a":2.86,"p":null} ``` Gate on confidence, not only on the label. `--json` gives the full distribution to `jq`. ```bash cat crash.txt | jev-code decide "Is this an error?" --choices yes,no --json \ | jq -e '.data.choice == "yes" and .data.confidence > 0.8' > /dev/null && open-ticket crash.txt ``` Grade many files in parallel with `xargs`. Large files need `--truncate`. ```bash ls docs/*.md | xargs -P 4 -I{} sh -c 'printf "%s\t" {}; jev-code decide --score "explains why, not only what" --truncate < {}' \ | sort -t"$(printf '\t')" -k2 -r ``` Read a run as data. `--json` emits every event. Select the low-confidence decisions. ```bash jev-code --print --json "write a number guessing game in game.py" \ | jq -r 'select(.type == "decision" and .data.confidence != null and .data.confidence < 0.6) | "\(.data.slot // .data.field // "action") → \(.data.choice) \(.data.confidence)"' ``` Replay a saved run and grep it. ```bash jev-code replay 810b329d-5869-4297-964e-320fd8907f23 --plain | grep '✗' ``` Reject a partial answer. A diff that does not fit stops with exit 125 unless `--truncate` is given, so a `&&` chain never commits what Jev did not read. ```bash git diff | jev-code decide --true "safe to commit" && git commit -am wip # decide: input is 61200 bytes; only 22976 fit. Pass --truncate to decide on the head alone. ``` ## FILES | Path | Content | | --- | --- | | `~/.config/jev-code/config.json` | The saved typesafe.ai API key. Mode 600. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `JEV_CODE_CONFIG_DIR` change the directory. | | `.env` | Optional. `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...` in the current directory. Loaded before the saved key. | | `.jev/runs/.jsonl` | One journal per run: every event as one JSON line. Input for `replay`. | | `.jev/eval/` | Eval records and journals from `pnpm run dev -- eval`. | ## EXIT STATUS | Command | Status | | --- | --- | | Session, `--print` | 0 when the run completes. 130 when cancelled. 1 for any other outcome. | | `decide --choices` | Index of the selected label. 125 on failure. | | `decide --true` | 0 at or above the threshold. 1 below it. 125 on failure. | | `decide --score`, `--spec` | 0. 125 on failure. | | `replay --plain` | 0. 130 on Ctrl-C. | ## LIMITS Jev has a 32k context and selects from bounded lists. Small programs complete. Larger programs can exhaust the request budget without a passing result. The eval ladder in `docs/guide.md` records the current state. Bash runs on your machine. Confirm each command unless you pass `--yes`. ## SEE ALSO [docs/sdk.md](docs/sdk.md) - public decisions, routers, programs, formal trees, limits, and package contract. [docs/guide.md](docs/guide.md) - CLI sessions, output formats, AST adapters, options, journals, and eval results. Based on the information above, please summarize and generate a comprehensive Repository Overview.

```
Repository Overview: jev-code

1. Project Purpose & Domain
---------------------------
`jev-code` (package `jev-code`, v0.2.0, ESM/TypeScript) is a decision-driven programming toolkit built around "Jev," a decision-only model served by typesafe.ai. Unlike text-generating coding assistants, Jev never emits free-form prose or code strings: it selects one option from a bounded list, returns a probability for a statement, or scores input against a rubric. The repository's central thesis is that code generation, tool use, and shell automation can be reformulated as a sequence of such constrained selections.

The project serves two audiences from one set of contracts:
- A TypeScript SDK for applications that want typed routing, composable decision programs, and validated formal-tree construction while retaining full ownership of side effects.
- A terminal coding agent (`jev-code` CLI) that builds programs production-by-production as abstract syntax trees, validates them with real compilers, executes them, and reports observed results.

The domain sits at the intersection of constrained/structured LLM decoding, program synthesis over formal grammars, and agentic CLI tooling.

2. Core Functionalities
-----------------------
- Typed decision SDK (`src/sdk/`): `DecisionSession` wraps a `DecisionProvider` with validation and resource accounting; `defineRouter`/`route` produce type-safe routers that map a model selection to a discriminated result; `DecisionProgram` (`program.ts`, with `node`, `value`, `parallel`, `fromInput`, `runProgram`) provides immutable, composable decision pipelines with final validators, cancellation, and event streams; `tree.ts` implements bounded formal-tree construction through `TreeSlot`, `branch`, `complete`, and `runTree`, where each slot is filled by choosing among grammar productions.
- Grammar-directed code synthesis: a full Python AST builder (`python-ast.ts`, `python-units.ts`, `python-search.ts` — functions, loops, conditionals, calls, imports, parallel helper units, multi-file packages), a Bash command AST (`bash-ast.ts` — programs, arguments, pipes, redirects, `&&`/`||`/`;`), and a shared imperative core (`lang/core.ts`) rendered into seven dialects: JavaScript, TypeScript, C, Rust, Go, Lua, and Ruby (`lang/*.ts`).
- Toolchain validation before write: every generated file is checked by its real validator (`python3` compile, `bash -n`, the TypeScript compiler, `gcc`/`clang -fsyntax-only`, `rustc --emit=metadata`, `go vet`, `luac -p`, `ruby -c`). A missing validator aborts the write. `test/lang-fuzz.test.ts` fuzzes every dialect with random productions and compiles the output.
- Fallback text decoding: for files without a grammar adapter, `scored-grid.ts`, `grid.ts`, and `structured-text.ts` implement character-alphabet scored-grid decoding and bounded text choices with syntax feedback.
- Agent harness (`harness.ts`): turn/request/step/time-budgeted run loop over built-in tools (`tools.ts` — atomic/staged file writes with undo, edits, sandboxed `bash` via `spawn` with a sanitized environment), workspace path confinement with symlink resolution (`workspace.ts`), and a per-run JSONL journal in `.jev/runs/<run-id>.jsonl`.
- Interactive terminal UI (`src/ui/`, Ink + React): a transcript of per-tool "cards," a live pane showing a file as it is built, a decision strip with the current slot, selected production, and confidence, and keystroke-level shell approval (`y` once, `n` deny, `a` grant for the session). Session slash-commands cover `/status`, `/files`, `/show`, `/trace`, `/plan`, `/history`, `/permissions`, `/paste`, `/cancel`, `/clear`, and host commands via `!<cmd>`.
- `decide` subcommand (`decide.ts`): a Unix-composable, tool-free, write-free decision filter over stdin, supporting `--choices` (exit status = index of the selected label), `--true` with `--threshold` (exit 0/1), `--score` over a four-level rubric, `--lines` for per-line ranking, `--spec file.json` for batched questions, `--json` for decision events, and `--truncate` for oversized input. Failures exit 125.
- Replay and observability: `replay.ts` and `ui/replay-session.ts` re-render saved journals through the same transcript (`--plain` for greppable output); `--json` emits one event per line; `summary.ts`, `diff.ts`, `print.ts`, `render-plain.ts`, and `timing.ts` handle presentation.
- Extensibility: `ast-adapters.ts` implements an `AstAdapter` interface and `AstRegistry` with `jev-code ast install|list|remove`, loading adapters from local paths or npm packages.
- Evaluation harness: `eval.ts` plus the `eval/` task suites (`file-io-script`, `guessing-game`, `multi-file-package`), each with a `task.json` and a programmatic `check.ts`, writing records and journals to `.jev/eval/`.

3. Architectural Composition
----------------------------
Layered, with the public surface deliberately narrow (package root export only; implementation paths are private):
- Public API layer — `src/index.ts` re-exports the harness, provider, tools, language adapters, eval, decide, and the whole `src/sdk/` surface.
- SDK/contract layer — `src/sdk/` (`decisions`, `program`, `router`, `tree`, `resources`, `validation`, `types`): provider-agnostic, effect-free primitives with resource limits, cancellation, and structured errors (`LimitError`, `DecisionError`, `CancelledError`, `ResourceExhaustedError`, `TreeDefinitionError`).
- Decision/provider layer — `provider.ts` (`JevProvider` over `TypeSafeClient.systemOne`), `decisions.ts` (state projection to JSON, request accounting), `decision-context.ts` (context windowing and pending-slot rendering).
- Generation layer — `generation.ts` orchestrates decoders, dispatching to AST adapters, scored grids, structured text, or bounded choices; `text-plan.ts` records plans.
- Language layer — `lang/` (shared core plus per-dialect renderers/validators) and the Python/Bash builders, all surfaced through the `AstAdapter` registry.
- Orchestration layer — `harness.ts` (run loop, tool dispatch, event emission, journaling) and `tools.ts` / `workspace.ts` / `env.ts` (effects and sandboxing).
- Presentation layer — `transcript.ts` (pure event → item model), `src/ui/*.tsx` (Ink components), `render-plain.ts`, `terminal-style.ts`.
- Entry layer — `cli.ts` (argument parsing, subcommands `decide`/`replay`/`login`/`logout`/`ast`), `config.ts` (key storage).
- Support — `docs/` (guide, SDK reference, dated plans and brainstorms), `examples/` (`router.ts`, `dependency-tree.ts`, `dialect-ast.mjs`, `add-task.md`), and a broad `test/` suite including fuzz tests, a baseline event fixture (`test/fixtures/events-baseline.jsonl`), UI tests, and a package-contract test that compiles consumer fixtures under both `bundler` and `nodenext` resolution.

4. Key Technologies & Frameworks
--------------------------------
TypeScript 5.9 targeting ES2023 with `NodeNext` modules and strict options (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noImplicitReturns`); Node.js ≥ 22 (the installer provisions a private Node 24 if needed); pnpm 10 as package manager; React 19 with Ink 7 and `ink-text-input` for the terminal UI; `tsx` as the dev runner and the Node built-in test runner (`tsx --test`) with `ink-testing-library` for UI assertions; the TypeScript compiler API used at runtime as a validator for JS/TS output; Node core APIs (`child_process`, `fs/promises`, `readline`, `string_decoder`, `crypto`) throughout.

5. Typical Usage & Workflow
---------------------------
SDK: install the package, implement or use `JevProvider`, construct a `DecisionSession`, then define a router (`defineRouter`/`route`), compose a `DecisionProgram`, or declare a formal tree of slots and productions, and run it with limits and a validator; the application performs any effects implied by the selection.

CLI: install via `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` and add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`. The first interactive run prompts for a typesafe.ai API key, stored mode-600 at `~/.config/jev-code/config.json` (overridable by `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or a local `.env`; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`JEV_CODE_CONFIG_DIR` relocate the directory). Run `jev-code` for an interactive session in the current directory, `jev-code "task"` to submit immediately, or `jev-code --print [--json] "task"` for one-shot/scripted runs. Shell commands require per-invocation confirmation unless `--yes` or `/permissions auto`. Runs journal to `.jev/runs/` for `jev-code replay <run-id>`. `jev-code decide` composes into shell pipelines — gating commits on a verdict, routing files by exit status, filtering or ranking log lines with `--lines`, and batch review via `--spec` piped to `jq`. Development uses `pnpm run dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and `pnpm run build`; `pnpm run dev -- eval` runs the eval ladder documented in `docs/guide.md`.

6. Dependencies & External Integrations
---------------------------------------
- `@typesafe-ai/sdk` (^0.6.0) — the sole model integration, used via `TypeSafeClient.systemOne` with a 30 s timeout and abort-signal support; requires a typesafe.ai API key.
- `ink`, `ink-text-input`, `react` — terminal rendering; `ink-testing-library` and `@types/react` in development.
- `typescript` as a runtime dependency (validator plus build), `tsx` and `@types/node` for development.
- External toolchains invoked on `PATH` as validators/runtimes: `python3`, `bash`, `gcc`/`clang`, `rustc`, `go`, `luac`, `ruby`; `asciinema` optionally replays the recorded demo session.
- Third-party AST adapter modules resolvable from a local path or npm via `jev-code ast install`.
- Local filesystem integrations: `~/.config/jev-code/config.json`, project-level `.env`, and the `.jev/` directory for run journals and eval records.

Known limits (as documented): Jev operates within a 32k context and always selects from bounded lists, so small programs complete reliably while larger ones can exhaust the request budget without a passing result; Bash executes on the host machine.
```
</solution>

Repository Overview: jev-code

1. Project Purpose & Domain
---------------------------
`jev-code` (package `jev-code`, v0.2.0, ESM/TypeScript) is a decision-driven programming toolkit built around "Jev," a decision-only model served by typesafe.ai. Unlike text-generating coding assistants, Jev never emits free-form prose or code strings: it selects one option from a bounded list, returns a probability for a statement, or scores input against a rubric. The repository's central thesis is that code generation, tool use, and shell automation can be reformulated as a sequence of such constrained selections.

The project serves two audiences from one set of contracts:
- A TypeScript SDK for applications that want typed routing, composable decision programs, and validated formal-tree construction while retaining full ownership of side effects.
- A terminal coding agent (`jev-code` CLI) that builds programs production-by-production as abstract syntax trees, validates them with real compilers, executes them, and reports observed results.

The domain sits at the intersection of constrained/structured LLM decoding, program synthesis over formal grammars, and agentic CLI tooling.

2. Core Functionalities
-----------------------
- Typed decision SDK (`src/sdk/`): `DecisionSession` wraps a `DecisionProvider` with validation and resource accounting; `defineRouter`/`route` produce type-safe routers that map a model selection to a discriminated result; `DecisionProgram` (`program.ts`, with `node`, `value`, `parallel`, `fromInput`, `runProgram`) provides immutable, composable decision pipelines with final validators, cancellation, and event streams; `tree.ts` implements bounded formal-tree construction through `TreeSlot`, `branch`, `complete`, and `runTree`, where each slot is filled by choosing among grammar productions.
- Grammar-directed code synthesis: a full Python AST builder (`python-ast.ts`, `python-units.ts`, `python-search.ts` — functions, loops, conditionals, calls, imports, parallel helper units, multi-file packages), a Bash command AST (`bash-ast.ts` — programs, arguments, pipes, redirects, `&&`/`||`/`;`), and a shared imperative core (`lang/core.ts`) rendered into seven dialects: JavaScript, TypeScript, C, Rust, Go, Lua, and Ruby (`lang/*.ts`).
- Toolchain validation before write: every generated file is checked by its real validator (`python3` compile, `bash -n`, the TypeScript compiler, `gcc`/`clang -fsyntax-only`, `rustc --emit=metadata`, `go vet`, `luac -p`, `ruby -c`). A missing validator aborts the write. `test/lang-fuzz.test.ts` fuzzes every dialect with random productions and compiles the output.
- Fallback text decoding: for files without a grammar adapter, `scored-grid.ts`, `grid.ts`, and `structured-text.ts` implement character-alphabet scored-grid decoding and bounded text choices with syntax feedback.
- Agent harness (`harness.ts`): turn/request/step/time-budgeted run loop over built-in tools (`tools.ts` — atomic/staged file writes with undo, edits, sandboxed `bash` via `spawn` with a sanitized environment), workspace path confinement with symlink resolution (`workspace.ts`), and a per-run JSONL journal in `.jev/runs/<run-id>.jsonl`.
- Interactive terminal UI (`src/ui/`, Ink + React): a transcript of per-tool "cards," a live pane showing a file as it is built, a decision strip with the current slot, selected production, and confidence, and keystroke-level shell approval (`y` once, `n` deny, `a` grant for the session). Session slash-commands cover `/status`, `/files`, `/show`, `/trace`, `/plan`, `/history`, `/permissions`, `/paste`, `/cancel`, `/clear`, and host commands via `!<cmd>`.
- `decide` subcommand (`decide.ts`): a Unix-composable, tool-free, write-free decision filter over stdin, supporting `--choices` (exit status = index of the selected label), `--true` with `--threshold` (exit 0/1), `--score` over a four-level rubric, `--lines` for per-line ranking, `--spec file.json` for batched questions, `--json` for decision events, and `--truncate` for oversized input. Failures exit 125.
- Replay and observability: `replay.ts` and `ui/replay-session.ts` re-render saved journals through the same transcript (`--plain` for greppable output); `--json` emits one event per line; `summary.ts`, `diff.ts`, `print.ts`, `render-plain.ts`, and `timing.ts` handle presentation.
- Extensibility: `ast-adapters.ts` implements an `AstAdapter` interface and `AstRegistry` with `jev-code ast install|list|remove`, loading adapters from local paths or npm packages.
- Evaluation harness: `eval.ts` plus the `eval/` task suites (`file-io-script`, `guessing-game`, `multi-file-package`), each with a `task.json` and a programmatic `check.ts`, writing records and journals to `.jev/eval/`.

3. Architectural Composition
----------------------------
Layered, with the public surface deliberately narrow (package root export only; implementation paths are private):
- Public API layer — `src/index.ts` re-exports the harness, provider, tools, language adapters, eval, decide, and the whole `src/sdk/` surface.
- SDK/contract layer — `src/sdk/` (`decisions`, `program`, `router`, `tree`, `resources`, `validation`, `types`): provider-agnostic, effect-free primitives with resource limits, cancellation, and structured errors (`LimitError`, `DecisionError`, `CancelledError`, `ResourceExhaustedError`, `TreeDefinitionError`).
- Decision/provider layer — `provider.ts` (`JevProvider` over `TypeSafeClient.systemOne`), `decisions.ts` (state projection to JSON, request accounting), `decision-context.ts` (context windowing and pending-slot rendering).
- Generation layer — `generation.ts` orchestrates decoders, dispatching to AST adapters, scored grids, structured text, or bounded choices; `text-plan.ts` records plans.
- Language layer — `lang/` (shared core plus per-dialect renderers/validators) and the Python/Bash builders, all surfaced through the `AstAdapter` registry.
- Orchestration layer — `harness.ts` (run loop, tool dispatch, event emission, journaling) and `tools.ts` / `workspace.ts` / `env.ts` (effects and sandboxing).
- Presentation layer — `transcript.ts` (pure event → item model), `src/ui/*.tsx` (Ink components), `render-plain.ts`, `terminal-style.ts`.
- Entry layer — `cli.ts` (argument parsing, subcommands `decide`/`replay`/`login`/`logout`/`ast`), `config.ts` (key storage).
- Support — `docs/` (guide, SDK reference, dated plans and brainstorms), `examples/` (`router.ts`, `dependency-tree.ts`, `dialect-ast.mjs`, `add-task.md`), and a broad `test/` suite including fuzz tests, a baseline event fixture (`test/fixtures/events-baseline.jsonl`), UI tests, and a package-contract test that compiles consumer fixtures under both `bundler` and `nodenext` resolution.

4. Key Technologies & Frameworks
--------------------------------
TypeScript 5.9 targeting ES2023 with `NodeNext` modules and strict options (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noImplicitReturns`); Node.js ≥ 22 (the installer provisions a private Node 24 if needed); pnpm 10 as package manager; React 19 with Ink 7 and `ink-text-input` for the terminal UI; `tsx` as the dev runner and the Node built-in test runner (`tsx --test`) with `ink-testing-library` for UI assertions; the TypeScript compiler API used at runtime as a validator for JS/TS output; Node core APIs (`child_process`, `fs/promises`, `readline`, `string_decoder`, `crypto`) throughout.

5. Typical Usage & Workflow
---------------------------
SDK: install the package, implement or use `JevProvider`, construct a `DecisionSession`, then define a router (`defineRouter`/`route`), compose a `DecisionProgram`, or declare a formal tree of slots and productions, and run it with limits and a validator; the application performs any effects implied by the selection.

CLI: install via `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` and add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`. The first interactive run prompts for a typesafe.ai API key, stored mode-600 at `~/.config/jev-code/config.json` (overridable by `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or a local `.env`; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`JEV_CODE_CONFIG_DIR` relocate the directory). Run `jev-code` for an interactive session in the current directory, `jev-code "task"` to submit immediately, or `jev-code --print [--json] "task"` for one-shot/scripted runs. Shell commands require per-invocation confirmation unless `--yes` or `/permissions auto`. Runs journal to `.jev/runs/` for `jev-code replay <run-id>`. `jev-code decide` composes into shell pipelines — gating commits on a verdict, routing files by exit status, filtering or ranking log lines with `--lines`, and batch review via `--spec` piped to `jq`. Development uses `pnpm run dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and `pnpm run build`; `pnpm run dev -- eval` runs the eval ladder documented in `docs/guide.md`.

6. Dependencies & External Integrations
---------------------------------------
- `@typesafe-ai/sdk` (^0.6.0) — the sole model integration, used via `TypeSafeClient.systemOne` with a 30 s timeout and abort-signal support; requires a typesafe.ai API key.
- `ink`, `ink-text-input`, `react` — terminal rendering; `ink-testing-library` and `@types/react` in development.
- `typescript` as a runtime dependency (validator plus build), `tsx` and `@types/node` for development.
- External toolchains invoked on `PATH` as validators/runtimes: `python3`, `bash`, `gcc`/`clang`, `rustc`, `go`, `luac`, `ruby`; `asciinema` optionally replays the recorded demo session.
- Third-party AST adapter modules resolvable from a local path or npm via `jev-code ast install`.
- Local filesystem integrations: `~/.config/jev-code/config.json`, project-level `.env`, and the `.jev/` directory for run journals and eval records.

Known limits (as documented): Jev operates within a 32k context and always selects from bounded lists, so small programs complete reliably while larger ones can exhaust the request budget without a passing result; Bash executes on the host machine.

Repository Overview: jev-code

1. Project Purpose & Domain
---------------------------
`jev-code` (package `jev-code`, v0.2.0, ESM/TypeScript) is a decision-driven programming toolkit built around "Jev," a decision-only model served by typesafe.ai. Unlike text-generating coding assistants, Jev never emits free-form prose or code strings: it selects one option from a bounded list, returns a probability for a statement, or scores input against a rubric. The repository's central thesis is that code generation, tool use, and shell automation can be reformulated as a sequence of such constrained selections.

The project serves two audiences from one set of contracts:
- A TypeScript SDK for applications that want typed routing, composable decision programs, and validated formal-tree construction while retaining full ownership of side effects.
- A terminal coding agent (`jev-code` CLI) that builds programs production-by-production as abstract syntax trees, validates them with real compilers, executes them, and reports observed results.

The domain sits at the intersection of constrained/structured LLM decoding, program synthesis over formal grammars, and agentic CLI tooling.

2. Core Functionalities
-----------------------
- Typed decision SDK (`src/sdk/`): `DecisionSession` wraps a `DecisionProvider` with validation and resource accounting; `defineRouter`/`route` produce type-safe routers that map a model selection to a discriminated result; `DecisionProgram` (`program.ts`, with `node`, `value`, `parallel`, `fromInput`, `runProgram`) provides immutable, composable decision pipelines with final validators, cancellation, and event streams; `tree.ts` implements bounded formal-tree construction through `TreeSlot`, `branch`, `complete`, and `runTree`, where each slot is filled by choosing among grammar productions.
- Grammar-directed code synthesis: a full Python AST builder (`python-ast.ts`, `python-units.ts`, `python-search.ts` — functions, loops, conditionals, calls, imports, parallel helper units, multi-file packages), a Bash command AST (`bash-ast.ts` — programs, arguments, pipes, redirects, `&&`/`||`/`;`), and a shared imperative core (`lang/core.ts`) rendered into seven dialects: JavaScript, TypeScript, C, Rust, Go, Lua, and Ruby (`lang/*.ts`).
- Toolchain validation before write: every generated file is checked by its real validator (`python3` compile, `bash -n`, the TypeScript compiler, `gcc`/`clang -fsyntax-only`, `rustc --emit=metadata`, `go vet`, `luac -p`, `ruby -c`). A missing validator aborts the write. `test/lang-fuzz.test.ts` fuzzes every dialect with random productions and compiles the output.
- Fallback text decoding: for files without a grammar adapter, `scored-grid.ts`, `grid.ts`, and `structured-text.ts` implement character-alphabet scored-grid decoding and bounded text choices with syntax feedback.
- Agent harness (`harness.ts`): turn/request/step/time-budgeted run loop over built-in tools (`tools.ts` — atomic/staged file writes with undo, edits, sandboxed `bash` via `spawn` with a sanitized environment), workspace path confinement with symlink resolution (`workspace.ts`), and a per-run JSONL journal in `.jev/runs/<run-id>.jsonl`.
- Interactive terminal UI (`src/ui/`, Ink + React): a transcript of per-tool "cards," a live pane showing a file as it is built, a decision strip with the current slot, selected production, and confidence, and keystroke-level shell approval (`y` once, `n` deny, `a` grant for the session). Repository Overview: jev-code

1. Project Purpose & Domain
---------------------------
`jev-code` (package `jev-code`, v0.2.0, ESM/TypeScript) is a decision-driven programming toolkit built around "Jev," a decision-only model served by typesafe.ai. Unlike text-generating coding assistants, Jev never emits free-form prose or code strings: it selects one option from a bounded list, returns a probability for a statement, or scores input against a rubric. The repository's central thesis is that code generation, tool use, and shell automation can be reformulated as a sequence of such constrained selections.

The project serves two audiences from one set of contracts:
- A TypeScript SDK for applications that want typed routing, composable decision programs, and validated formal-tree construction while retaining full ownership of side effects.
- A terminal coding agent (`jev-code` CLI) that builds programs production-by-production as abstract syntax trees, validates them with real compilers, executes them, and reports observed results.

The domain sits at the intersection of constrained/structured LLM decoding, program synthesis over formal grammars, and agentic CLI tooling.

2. Core Functionalities
-----------------------
- Typed decision SDK (`src/sdk/`): `DecisionSession` wraps a `DecisionProvider` with validation and resource accounting; `defineRouter`/`route` produce type-safe routers that map a model selection to a discriminated result; `DecisionProgram` (`program.ts`, with `node`, `value`, `parallel`, `fromInput`, `runProgram`) provides immutable, composable decision pipelines with final validators, cancellation, and event streams; `tree.ts` implements bounded formal-tree construction through `TreeSlot`, `branch`, `complete`, and `runTree`, where each slot is filled by choosing among grammar productions.
- Grammar-directed code synthesis: a full Python AST builder (`python-ast.ts`, `python-units.ts`, `python-search.ts` — functions, loops, conditionals, calls, imports, parallel helper units, multi-file packages), a Bash command AST (`bash-ast.ts` — programs, arguments, pipes, redirects, `&&`/`||`/`;`), and a shared imperative core (`lang/core.ts`) rendered into seven dialects: JavaScript, TypeScript, C, Rust, Go, Lua, and Ruby (`lang/*.ts`).
- Toolchain validation before write: every generated file is checked by its real validator (`python3` compile, `bash -n`, the TypeScript compiler, `gcc`/`clang -fsyntax-only`, `rustc --emit=metadata`, `go vet`, `luac -p`, `ruby -c`). A missing validator aborts the write. `test/lang-fuzz.test.ts` fuzzes every dialect with random productions and compiles the output.
- Fallback text decoding: for files without a grammar adapter, `scored-grid.ts`, `grid.ts`, and `structured-text.ts` implement character-alphabet scored-grid decoding and bounded text choices with syntax feedback.
- Agent harness (`harness.ts`): turn/request/step/time-budgeted run loop over built-in tools (`tools.ts` — atomic/staged file writes with undo, edits, sandboxed `bash` via `spawn` with a sanitized environment), workspace path confinement with symlink resolution (`workspace.ts`), and a per-run JSONL journal in `.jev/runs/<run-id>.jsonl`.
- Interactive terminal UI (`src/ui/`, Ink + React): a transcript of per-tool "cards," a live pane showing a file as it is built, a decision strip with the current slot, selected production, and confidence, and keystroke-level shell approval (`y` once, `n` deny, `a` grant for the session). Session slash-commands cover `/status`, `/files`, `/show`, `/trace`, `/plan`, `/history`, `/permissions`, `/paste`, `/cancel`, `/clear`, and host commands via `!<cmd>`.
- `decide` subcommand (`decide.ts`): a Unix-composable, tool-free, write-free decision filter over stdin, supporting `--choices` (exit status = index of the selected label), `--true` with `--threshold` (exit 0/1), `--score` over a four-level rubric, `--lines` for per-line ranking, `--spec file.json` for batched questions, `--json` for decision events, and `--truncate` for oversized input. Failures exit 125.
- Replay and observability: `replay.ts` and `ui/replay-session.ts` re-render saved journals through the same transcript (`--plain` for greppable output); `--json` emits one event per line; `summary.ts`, `diff.ts`, `print.ts`, `render-plain.ts`, and `timing.ts` handle presentation.

3. Architectural Composition
----------------------------
Layered, with the public surface deliberately narrow (package root export only; implementation paths are private):
- Public API layer — `src/index.ts` re-exports the harness, provider, tools, language adapters, eval, decide, and the whole `src/sdk/` surface.

- Orchestration layer — `harness.ts` (run loop, tool dispatch, event emission, journaling) and `tools.ts` / `workspace.ts` / `env.ts` (effects and sandboxing).

---------------------------
SDK: install the package, implement or use `JevProvider`, construct a `DecisionSession`, then define a router (`defineRouter`/`route`), compose a `DecisionProgram`, or declare a formal tree of slots and productions, and run it with limits and a validator; the application performs any effects implied by the selection.

CLI: install via `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` and add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`. Development uses `pnpm run dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and `pnpm run build`; `pnpm run dev -- eval` runs the eval ladder documented in `docs/guide.md`.

---------------------------------------
- `@typesafe-ai/sdk` (^0.6.0) — the sole model integration, used via `TypeSafeClient.systemOne` with a 30 s timeout and abort-signal support; requires a typesafe.ai API key.

- Local filesystem integrations: `~/.config/jev-code/config.json`, project-level `.env`, and the `.jev/` directory for run journals and eval records.

Known limits (as documented): Jev operates within a 32k context and always selects from bounded lists, so small programs complete reliably while larger ones can exhaust the request budget without a passing result; Bash executes on the host machine.

Repository Overview: jev-code

1. Project Purpose & Domain
---------------------------
`jev-code` (package `jev-code`, v0.2.0, ESM/TypeScript) is a decision-driven programming toolkit built around "Jev," a decision-only model served by typesafe.ai. Unlike text-generating coding assistants, Jev never emits free-form prose or code strings: it selects one option from a bounded list, returns a probability for a statement, or scores input against a rubric. The repository's central thesis is that code generation, tool use, and shell automation can be reformulated as a sequence of such constrained selections.

The project serves two audiences from one set of contracts:
- A TypeScript SDK for applications that want typed routing, composable decision programs, and validated formal-tree construction while retaining full ownership of side effects.
- A terminal coding agent (`jev-code` CLI) that builds programs production-by-production as abstract syntax trees, validates them with real compilers, executes them, and reports observed results.

The domain sits at the intersection of constrained/structured LLM decoding, program synthesis over formal grammars, and agentic CLI tooling.

2. Core Functionalities
-----------------------
- Typed decision SDK (`src/sdk/`): `DecisionSession` wraps a `DecisionProvider` with validation and resource accounting; `defineRouter`/`route` produce type-safe routers that map a model selection to a discriminated result; `DecisionProgram` (`program.ts`, with `node`, `value`, `parallel`, `fromInput`, `runProgram`) provides immutable, composable decision pipelines with final validators, cancellation, and event streams; `tree.ts` implements bounded formal-tree construction through `TreeSlot`, `branch`, `complete`, and `runTree`, where each slot is filled by choosing among grammar productions.
- Grammar-directed code synthesis: a full Python AST builder (`python-ast.ts`, `python-units.ts`, `python-search.ts` — functions, loops, conditionals, calls, imports, parallel helper units, multi-file packages), a Bash command AST (`bash-ast.ts` — programs, arguments, pipes, redirects, `&&`/`||`/`;`), and a shared imperative core (`lang/core.ts`) rendered into seven dialects: JavaScript, TypeScript, C, Rust, Go, Lua, and Ruby (`lang/*.ts`).
- Toolchain validation before write: every generated file is checked by its real validator (`python3` compile, `bash -n`, the TypeScript compiler, `gcc`/`clang -fsyntax-only`, `rustc --emit=metadata`, `go vet`, `luac -p`, `ruby -c`). A missing validator aborts the write. `test/lang-fuzz.test.ts` fuzzes every dialect with random productions and compiles the output.
- Fallback text decoding: for files without a grammar adapter, `scored-grid.ts`, `grid.ts`, and `structured-text.ts` implement character-alphabet scored-grid decoding and bounded text choices with syntax feedback.
- Agent harness (`harness.ts`): turn/request/step/time-budgeted run loop over built-in tools (`tools.ts` — atomic/staged file writes with undo, edits, sandboxed `bash` via `spawn` with a sanitized environment), workspace path confinement with symlink resolution (`workspace.ts`), and a per-run JSONL journal in `.jev/runs/<run-id>.jsonl`.
- Interactive terminal UI (`src/ui/`, Ink + React): a transcript of per-tool "cards," a live pane showing a file as it is built, a decision strip with the current slot, selected production, and confidence, and keystroke-level shell approval (`y` once, `n` deny, `a` grant for the session). Session slash-commands cover `/status`, `/files`, `/show`, `/trace`, `/plan`, `/history`, `/permissions`, `/paste`, `/cancel`, `/clear`, and host commands via `!<cmd>`.
- `decide` subcommand (`decide.ts`): a Unix-composable, tool-free, write-free decision filter over stdin, supporting `--choices` (exit status = index of the selected label), `--true` with `--threshold` (exit 0/1), `--score` over a four-level rubric, `--lines` for per-line ranking, `--spec file.json` for batched questions, `--json` for decision events, and `--truncate` for oversized input. Failures exit 125.

3. Architectural Composition
----------------------------
Layered, with the public surface deliberately narrow (package root export only; implementation paths are private):
- Public API layer — `src/index.ts` re-exports the harness, provider, tools, language adapters, eval, decide, and the whole `src/sdk/` surface.

- Orchestration layer — `harness.ts` (run loop, tool dispatch, event emission, journaling) and `tools.ts` / `workspace.ts` / `env.ts` (effects and sandboxing).

5. Typical Usage & Workflow
---------------------------
SDK: install the package, implement or use `JevProvider`, construct a `DecisionSession`, then define a router (`defineRouter`/`route`), compose a `DecisionProgram`, or declare a formal tree of slots and productions, and run it with limits and a validator; the application performs any effects implied by the selection.

CLI: install via `curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash` and add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`. The first interactive run prompts for a typesafe.ai API key, stored mode-600 at `~/.config/jev-code/config.json` (overridable by `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or a local `.env`; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`JEV_CODE_CONFIG_DIR` relocate the directory). Run `jev-code` for an interactive session in the current directory, `jev-code "task"` to submit immediately, or `jev-code --print [--json] "task"` for one-shot/scripted runs. Development uses `pnpm run dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and `pnpm run build`; `pnpm run dev -- eval` runs the eval ladder documented in `docs/guide.md`.

---------------------------------------
- `@typesafe-ai/sdk` (^0.6.0) — the sole model integration, used via `TypeSafeClient.systemOne` with a 30 s timeout and abort-signal support; requires a typesafe.ai API key.

- Local filesystem integrations: `~/.config/jev-code/config.json`, project-level `.env`, and the `.jev/` directory for run journals and eval records.

Known limits (as documented): Jev operates within a 32k context and always selects from bounded lists, so small programs complete reliably while larger ones can exhaust the request budget without a passing result; Bash executes on the host machine.
